persona: Same MBA student, analyzing a client's online-store order data for a marketing-analytics course project on channel performance
source_style: exported order-level data from the Shopify admin for April, then again for May, and pasted the two monthly CSV exports together in Excel before re-saving as one CSV

columns.name: OrderID
columns.notes: ORD-1001..ORD-1090, sequential by creation order (not by date); one order (ORD-1023) appears twice

columns.name: OrderDate
columns.notes: Rows 1-45 (April, US-locale export) use M/D/YYYY text; rows after the repeated header (May export) use YYYY-MM-DD; the same underlying dates in canonical form are April/May 2026

columns.name: Channel
columns.notes: Online Store / Instagram Ads / Retail Partner / Email Campaign

columns.name: Region
columns.notes: West / Midwest / Northeast / South; 4 rows have the value missing, written inconsistently as empty string or literal 'N/A'

columns.name: UnitPrice
columns.notes: USD unit price from a fixed catalog {19.99,24.99,29.99,34.99,44.99,54.99}; 8 scattered rows were hand-edited and show it as currency text with a $ and thousands comma instead of a plain number

columns.name: Discount_pct
columns.notes: Percent off (0/10/15/20/25); when 0, most rows leave the cell blank but 4 rows instead show a literal '-' -- neither means missing, both mean no discount

columns.name: TotalRevenue
columns.notes: = UnitsSold * UnitPrice * (1 - Discount_pct/100), rounded to cents; same 8 rows as UnitPrice are hand-edited to currency text with $ and thousands comma

columns.name: PaymentMethod
columns.notes: Credit Card / PayPal / Apple Pay / Gift Card

clean_table.rule: 45 April-2026 orders + 45 May-2026 orders (90 total), OrderID=ORD-1001..ORD-1090 assigned in creation order then each month's rows sorted by date for export (mirroring how Shopify exports one month at a time, date-ascending). Channel ~ weighted choice over 4 categories [45,20,25,10]; Region ~ weighted choice [30,25,25,20]; UnitsSold ~ Uniform{1..5}; UnitPrice ~ Uniform choice over catalog {19.99,24.99,29.99,34.99,44.99,54.99}; Discount_pct ~ weighted choice over {0(x3 weight),10,15,20,25} (0 is 3x as likely as any other single value); TotalRevenue = round(UnitsSold*UnitPrice*(1-Discount_pct/100),2); PaymentMethod ~ weighted choice [55,25,15,5]. Seed=20260922. The physical file additionally contains: a second copy of the header row where the May export was pasted in, one duplicated order row (ORD-1023, the April order at true index 22, repeated once more near the end), and a bottom 'TOTAL' row (OrderID='TOTAL', UnitsSold=sum of all 90 UnitsSold, TotalRevenue=sum of all 90 TotalRevenue formatted as currency text) -- none of these three extra physical rows are real orders beyond the 90 above.

intended_analysis: Does average order value (TotalRevenue) differ by marketing channel (one-way ANOVA / Kruskal-Wallis across Online Store / Instagram Ads / Retail Partner / Email Campaign)? Is there a relationship between discount percentage and units sold? Did total revenue grow from April to May?
mess_applied: File is two monthly exports pasted together, so the header row ('OrderID,OrderDate,...') appears twice in the file -- once at the very top and once again where May's export begins
OrderDate format changes partway through the file: M/D/YYYY for the April block, YYYY-MM-DD for the May block, because the two monthly exports used different locale settings
UnitPrice and TotalRevenue are plain numbers for most rows but currency-formatted text (e.g. "$1,234.50") for 8 scattered rows that were manually re-typed
Discount_pct uses two different conventions for 'no discount': a blank cell in most rows, a literal '-' character in 4 rows
Region is missing for 4 rows, written inconsistently as an empty string in some and the literal text 'N/A' in others
One order (ORD-1023) is duplicated -- its row appears a second time near the May/duplicate boundary from a copy-paste while merging the two files
A spurious 'TOTAL' row with column sums sits at the very bottom, left over from an Excel SUM() column the student added before re-exporting
File is saved with a UTF-8 byte-order mark (Excel's default 'CSV UTF-8' save) and has two trailing blank lines at the end
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: A reader that doesn't detect the repeated header line would ingest it as a bogus data row (all-text 'OrderDate' etc. breaking numeric parsing for that row); naively parsing OrderDate as one fixed format would either error or silently misread month/day for one of the two blocks (e.g. 4/3/2026 vs 2026-05-04 ambiguity); summing TotalRevenue including the bottom TOTAL row would double the true total; not deduping ORD-1023 would inflate n to 91 (plus the TOTAL row makes 92 apparent rows) instead of the true 90 orders; treating blank and '-' as different discount values (rather than both = 0) would create a spurious category.
